meta.title: Use gemini-flash-lite model for app name and commit message generation
meta.body_summary: Switch the LLM model used for app name and commit message generation to gemini-flash-lite to improve performance, with a dedicated client for these operations.

perf_labels.notes: Devin switched model to gemini-flash-lite in agent_session.py; reviewer approved without benchmarking; merged after cache-file cleanup.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 966 changed lines, the PR appears medium-sized by absolute volume, but over 900 lines are in cache JSON artifacts; the actual performance change is only 5 lines in agent_session.py. This is a tiny, low-risk model swap that merged quickly and fits the outcome.

review_details.concern_detail: No concerns raised; reviewer approved with no feedback.
review_details.performance_claim: Use the faster gemini-flash-lite model instead of the default model for app name and commit message generation to improve latency.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Switching a model string in an LLM client configuration is trivial; the PR was approved instantly with no requirement for performance benchmarks.

detection_detail.code_reading: Reviewer likely inspected the diff and approved without comments; the change is a single model name string replacement in one file.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No benchmarks, measurements, or repro steps provided; only a narrative claim that gemini-flash-lite is faster.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: No performance regression issues were raised; a cache file added by Devin was reverted and replaced by the maintainer, but that was a build artifact correction.

core_change_summary.description: In agent/trpc_agent/agent_session.py, the LLM client is now initialized with 'gemini-flash-lite' for app name and commit message generation; the rest of the session uses the default model. The core change is only 3 added lines and 2 deleted lines.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Large churn in cache JSON files (over 900 lines) is unrelated to the performance improvement; they appeared due to model cache generation and were later corrected.
